passages: "Our cat ran away once, and he brought her back, and we talked over the fence, and were getting on capitally, all about cricket, and so on, when he saw Meg coming, and walked off. I mean to know him some day, for he needs fun, I'm sure he does," said Jo decidedly.

Oh, dear, yes, he liked it amazingly! And was so touched and pleased by that confiding little kiss that all his crustiness vanished, and he just set her on his knee, and laid his wrinkled cheek against her rosy one, feeling as if he had got his own little granddaughter back again.
It did not seem at all comical to Meg, who kissed and caressed the afflicted heroine in the tenderest manner.
Then he amused her for an hour, and was much interested in all her trials.
"I don't think I like it only because it's so pretty, but I want to wear it as the girl in the story wore her bracelet, to remind me of something."

Beth helped her dress, and made a charming little wreath for her hair, while Jo astonished her family by getting herself up with unusual care, and hinting darkly that the tables were about to be turned.
"You never shall be again," broke in Laurie, putting his arm about her, as if to fence out every human ill.
Everyone greeted him kindly, for Jo's sake at first, but very soon they liked him for his own.
